title: Rahul Gandhi Detained Outside Modi's Home Amid India Exam Protest
excerpt: Delhi police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other opposition figures during a sit-in protest demanding the resignation of PM Modi and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam leaks and a crackdown on student demonstrators.
body:
• Delhi Police detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other opposition leaders during a sit-in protest outside PM Modi's residence on Tuesday
  • The protest followed Monday's violent clashes between police and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demonstrators marching on Parliament, which left nearly 180 people injured
  • Opposition leaders demanded the resignations of PM Modi, Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and Home Minister Amit Shah over exam paper leaks and the police crackdown
  • Modi broke his silence on the exam crisis, saying through a cabinet minister that "strongest possible steps" were being taken to protect students' interests

Delhi Police on Tuesday detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, and several other opposition leaders as they staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's official residence on Lok Kalyan Marg. The opposition figures were demanding accountability for Monday's violent police crackdown on student protesters and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over national exam paper leaks.

Television footage broadcast by ANI showed Gandhi, dressed in his signature white T-shirt and khaki trousers, lying on the road and resisting police attempts to remove him before being placed on a bus along with other detained Congress members. Congress leader Pawan Khera told reporters that police did not inform the party where Gandhi was being taken.

"An attack on students is an attack on every Indian family. PM Modi believes he can get away without answers, without consequences. He cannot. Not this time."

— Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader

A Day After Violent Clashes

The opposition protest came a day after a Cockroach Janta Party-led march toward Parliament descended into violent clashes between demonstrators and police. Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were injured, including 118 security personnel and 60 protesters, after officers used baton charges and tear gas to disperse the crowd. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said more than 150 protesters were undergoing hospital treatment, though Reuters could not independently verify the figures.

https://x.com/NewsWireLK/status/2079641980804452490

On Tuesday, more than 5,000 protesters returned to Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site, the movement's base since it grew from an online satire into a mass youth mobilization. The CJP said it would continue its anti-government protest but would not march on Parliament again, fearing further police violence against its supporters.

The movement, which has drawn millions of Gen Z supporters, centers on the leaking of question papers for the NEET medical entrance examination in May — a scandal that affected roughly 2 million students and, according to local media, led about a dozen to take their own lives.

Modi Breaks Silence

In his first public comments on the exam crisis, Modi told lawmakers of his ruling alliance that the government had acted immediately on reports of irregularities. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju relayed that 13 people had been arrested and jailed, and that a re-examination had been successfully conducted.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=YYNUBrc3dX8

"The prime minister said that to ensure the future of youth is not jeopardised, everyone should unite to ensure strict steps are taken, those guilty punished, and a foolproof system is created."

— Kiren Rijiju, Parliamentary Affairs Minister

The CJP's three demands remain the release of activist Sonam Wangchuk — the Magsaysay Award winner who began a hunger strike on June 28 and was forcibly hospitalized by police on Saturday — Pradhan's resignation, and compensation of 10 million rupees ($104,000) each for families of students who died by suicide. On Tuesday, the Delhi High Court ordered that Wangchuk be shifted to a private hospital, fulfilling one of those demands.

Opposition Seizes a Rare Opening

The solidarity with student protesters could prove politically significant. Leaders from nearly all opposition parties — including NCP's Supriya Sule, NCP chief Sharad Pawar, and AAP's Arvind Kejriwal — joined or voiced support for the protest, making it the broadest opposition mobilization in months.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DY9V89CgK0A/

Analysts noted that India's under-30 population, estimated at more than half of the country's 1.42 billion people, represents a substantial electoral bloc frustrated by persistent unemployment despite years of economic growth. With state elections approaching in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh next year, the political stakes are high.

"There is now a one-upmanship among political parties over who can best position themselves as the champion of India's youth," said Rasheed Kidwai, a political analyst and visiting fellow with the Observer Research Foundation. "Every political party is acting according to its own electoral calculations."

The CJP has welcomed opposition support while insisting the movement remains non-partisan. "It's not a political protest. It's a movement of the masses," a CJP spokesperson said, adding that the party had invited opposition leaders to show solidarity.

What's Next

The exam protest movement, now the biggest challenge of Modi's third term, shows no signs of abating. Priyanka Gandhi was released from detention hours later after former Congress president Sonia Gandhi arrived at Mandir Marg Police Station. The CJP plans to continue its Jantar Mantar sit-in, while Health Minister J.P. Nadda has reportedly sought time to discuss the protesters' demands within the government.

Whether the opposition's involvement sustains or dilutes the student-led movement remains an open question. Political analyst Sandeep Shastri warned: "If political parties join this movement, there is a strong chance that the leaders who actually started it, as well as the issues driving it, will take a back seat."
image_caption: Rahul Gandhi sits on the road outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence as police attempt to remove him during Tuesday's protest. The Congress leader was demanding answers over police action against student demonstrators and the resignation of the education minister.
nri_angle: The political crisis over exam integrity and youth unemployment resonates directly with Indian diaspora families weighing educational pathways and career prospects for children in India.
